messages:
devin: Heads-up — saw ~35% drop in prefix cache hit rate after last night's runtime rollout (kernel v2.14 + quant profile B).

maria: Numbers?

devin: Snapshot from per-route:

```
route: /v1/generate
pre-rollout hit_rate: 0.71
post-rollout hit_rate: 0.46
kv_cache_hits: 214k -> 140k
avg_first_token_latency: 36ms -> 58ms
```

aj: Did the rollout include fused-attn + tokenizer normalizer change?

devin: Yes (build 2026-03-17-b52). Traces point to key generation mismatch during warmup.

perfbot: Auto-check: sampled key diffs (n=50) -> 18% show trailing "\u0000" or altered normalization.

maria: Paste concrete pair?

devin: 

```
pre_key: ctx-v2|sha1:8f3a|tok-norm|len:64
post_key: ctx-v2|sha1:8f3a\u0000|tok-norm-v2|len:64
```

devin: Tokenizer appended a version tag and runtime zero-padding leaked into canonical form.

aj: So exact-string keys break. Any effect on batching?

devin: Yes — miss storm pushed traffic to cold path, median batch size in first 300ms dropped 4 -> 2.

perfbot: Profiling snippets:

```
# post-rollout
00:00.120 serve_request -> cache_lookup -> MISS
00:00.121 run_infer_kernel(attn_fused_v2)
00:00.180 populate_kv_cache
00:00.181 return

# pre-rollout
00:00.120 serve_request -> cache_lookup -> HIT
00:00.121 fast_path_kv_read
00:00.122 return
```

aj: Mitigations?

devin: Short term: shim to canonicalize keys (strip trailing nulls, drop tok-norm suffix). Local test raises hit_rate to ~0.67 on sampled traffic.

maria: Can you canary that with fused-attn kept? We want to keep kernel perf if possible.

devin: Launching 5% canary with shim. @maria monitor SLOs and warmup curves.

perfbot: Canary started at 1732109970; will run 2h and aggregate.

maria: Enabled kv eviction debug logs for the canary.

aj: Long term: formalize a stable key schema, add property tests, and consider migration tool to rehydrate old keys.

devin: Filed PERF-1298 with reproducer and patch: https://redwood.internal/perf/1298

sre-ops: FYI alerting thresholds auto-snoozed for canary window (tracked in incident-ops).

aj: Good find. Looks like a keying + padding interaction. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
